newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 30.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- PUBLIC WARY OF TORY TAX CUTS, SAYS CLARKE

The Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has expressed the opinion that he does not necessarily need to institute reductions in taxation in the next budget in order to improve the standing of the Conservatives in the polls. He added that the failure to deliver on previous promises of tax cuts has left the voters suspicious. Observers believe that cuts are also made less certain by other problems being encountered in trimming public spending.
-- JARDINE FLEMING HEAD QUIT OVER REFORMS

Alan Smith, who has resigned as head of investment bank Jardine Fleming, has claimed that his departure has been the result of a dispute over restructuring in the wake of a fund management scandal at the bank. He was reported to have been concerned that changes to management structure in the wake of heavy fines relating to the diversion of funds into the personal account of fund manager Colin Armstrong, would have a detrimental impact on Jardine Fleming's ability to compete in Asian markets.
-- VOICE SOUGHT FOR OLIVETTI INVESTORS

A number of investors in the troubled Italian computer group Olivetti are reported to have suggested that a Milanese lawyer, Dario Trevisan, be appointed to the board of the company in order to represent their interests. Investors in Olivetti have been attempting to extract more detail from the company regarding its financial state since recent speculation that figures did not represent the true state of affairs, prompting sharp falls in its share price.
-- PRIVATE FINANCE PLANS FOR HOSPITALS FACE COLLAPSE

The head of the private finance unit of the NHS, Andrew Neill, has admitted that government plans to use the Private Finance Initiative to help fund the construction of NHS hospitals will have to be scrapped. The warning, seen as an embarrassment to the government, comes in the wake of similar expressions of caution from the head of the NHS Trust Federation. Many trusts are reported to be unable to meet the annual payments to private companies which such contracts would require.
-- LEADING APPLIANCE MAKERS WARN

European electrical appliance manufacturers Electrolux and Whirlpool have warned that changes in local purchasing patterns are likely to impact adversely on their results for the third quarter. Both companies have noted that European consumers have been purchasing fewer appliances and those that are buying are opting for less expensive items. The warnings come in the wake
of a series of drops in European demand.
-- BRITISH GAS DEAL WITH SCOTTISH HYDRO FAILS

It has emerged that a proposed sale by British Gas of some of its business interests in Scotland and the north of England to Scottish Hydro has failed as a result of the considerable regulatory pressure under which the former currently finds itself. The problems affecting the deal were compounded by errors that have occurred with a new computerized billing system at British Gas. The deal, had it gone ahead, would have resulted in the creation of the country's
second-largest gas company.
-- SPANISH PREMIER PLEDGES TO MEET EMU CONDITIONS

Spanish prime minister Jose Maria Aznar has stated that his country is prepared to take whatever measures are deemed necessary in 1997 in order to meet Maastricht conditions for participation in the single European currency. At the same time the Spanish premier warned against the issue being allowed to create division between the north and south of the European Union.
-- EU IN ACCORD ON TELECOMS LICENSING

Telecommunications ministers from across the EU have reached agreement on how operators will be licensed after the sector is liberalized in 1998. The accord is aimed at ensuring that international and EU-based companies face as few bureaucratic barriers to participation in the market as possible and that a single market in telecoms services is forged. A number of conditions have been agreed relating to the criteria under which licenses will be issued by member states.
-- DEHAEHE PLANS EMU BUDGET

As part of a drive to meet Maastricht criteria for participation in the single European currency the Belgian government is planning to make use of 5 billion sterling in foreign currency reserves to reduce its public debt level. The government is also planning to announce a range of cuts to benefits and pensions in an effort to cut spending. During the summer the country's premier secured temporary rights to rule by decree on budgetary matters.
-- US AND EU TO ELIMINATE TARIFFS ON IT

In an 11th-hour agreement members of the Quad group of nations meeting in Seattle have agreed a compromise that should keep on track efforts to secure a WTO accord on the lowering of international tariffs in the information technology sector. A dispute over access for the EU to a US/Japanese bilateral pact in this field had threatened to derail wider negotiations. The EU has now agreed to eliminate its tariffs on semiconductors prior to being accorded membership of the World Semiconductor Council, established by the US and Japan. BMC +44-171-377-1742
